nodes.label: docs/canon/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md — how a row leaves `unreviewed`: the verdict block, the four verdicts, what counts as evidence, mandatory falsification, and the blackout rule. Binding on whoever works REVIEW_WORKLIST.md

One item at a time: work REVIEW_WORKLIST.md in its printed order, one row, one verdict, then stop and hand it over. No batch verdicts — "the following twelve are all fine" is not twelve verdicts, it is zero. A verdict covers exactly one id; two rows may share a check command but never a verdict. The protocol is itself interpretation and cannot be cited as evidence for anything, including its own authority

The verdict block, where a field left out voids the verdict: CLAIM (quoted verbatim from the surface), KIND (intent | state), CHECK (the exact command run), OUTPUT (pasted verbatim, including "0 hit(s)" and including errors), QUOTE (intent claims only — the user's words verbatim with date and the corpus line user_turns_all.jsonl L###), REFUTE, SEARCHED, RETURNED, VERDICT, PROPOSED. OUTPUT is pasted, never described — "the search confirms it" is not output, "0 hit(s)" is

Only four verdicts exist: `supported` (evidence found and pasted; for intent, a corpus quote with its line), `unsupported` (looked, in a window where the record is dense, found nothing), `contradicted` (the record says otherwise, both sides quoted), `cannot-determine` (cannot be settled from available evidence, and names what is missing). "Looks reasonable", "probably fine", "seems grounded", "consistent with the design" are not verdicts, and a review that produces one has produced nothing

The blackout rule: the corpus runs 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-03, nothing survives before 05-14, and 05-16 → 05-26 and 05-29 → 06-26 hold zero turns. A claim whose support would sit in those windows returns zero hits by construction — that is `cannot-determine — corpus blackout <dates>`, never `unsupported`. Not theoretical: CQ "MY WORDS ARE THE CANON" and CQ "only RAGAS" both return 0 hits, and both are cited in CANON_AUDIT.md with 06-25 dates inside the second blackout as [DOC] recoveries

What counts as evidence: only the corpus (docs/canon/raw/user_turns_all.jsonl, cited by line number), git (commits, diffs, `git show <ref>:<path>` bytes), code read with file:line, data and run outputs under v3/output/, and the output of a command run this session. Never evidence, for anything: CANON_AUDIT.md, DESIGN_HISTORY.md, OPEN_DECISIONS.md, USER_CANON.md, REVIEW_REGISTER.md, REVIEW_WORKLIST.md, the protocol itself, any state or handoff doc, any memory file on either machine, any agent definition, CLAUDE.md, either README, DATA_README.md, raw/git_record.md, raw/desktop_docs_record.md, any report an agent wrote

USER_CANON.md is not the corpus. It is 469 agent-selected quotes, 115 of them second-hand [DOC] recoveries. Quote the turn from user_turns_all.jsonl with its line number; if a quote appears in USER_CANON.md and not in the corpus, that is a finding about USER_CANON.md. The worklist's audit prior column is one agent's opinion printed for context — it is not a starting position, it does not shift the burden, and a verdict that agrees with it needs exactly the same evidence as one that does not

Falsification is mandatory and goes on the record. Confirming a claim is not reviewing it: REFUTE states, before searching, what evidence would make the claim false — a claim you cannot say how to falsify is `cannot-determine — unfalsifiable as worded`; SEARCHED goes looking for that specific counter-evidence, not for support; RETURNED pastes what came back, including when it returned nothing. For an intent claim the refutation search is usually the user saying the opposite; for a state claim it is usually the code or the run output disagreeing with the doc

The four data files v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl and 10smoke.jsonl are not to be opened — 2026-08-02: "honestly, you should not have the questions/gold available to you, there is 0% good that can come out of taht". Rows whose natural check would open one are marked [user-gated] in the worklist: propose the check, name the indirect route where one exists (per-type fields are re-joined into eval_results.jsonl at eval time), and hand it over. Do not open the file and do not ask an agent to open it for you

The agent proposes; the user rules. Nothing is marked `reviewed` — status changes are the user's, in the user's own words. No file is edited because a verdict says it is wrong: the verdict is the deliverable. Nothing is deleted. A verdict of `contradicted` on a hard rule does not suspend the rule, it goes to the user. Where two of the user's own statements conflict, both stand — do not pick a winner, do not reconcile them, do not build to one and record the other as superseded; report the conflict

How a session opens: the first substantive output of any session is item 1 with its evidence. Not before it — no summary of the pile, no count of what is left, no recommended order (the worklist already encodes the order, by enforcement power), no plan, no inventory of the list in any form at any length. Given a list, the lazy move is to summarise it and propose a sequence: fluent, confident, and evidence-free. If the list is picked up mid-way, the first output is the next `unreviewed` row's verdict block

The one-glance check: every verdict shows a command and its output, and that is the whole audit. A verdict without pasted output is void whether or not anyone notices, and the reviewer says so itself rather than waiting to be caught — a check that could not be run reads CHECK <command> / OUTPUT NOT RUN — <why> / VERDICT cannot-determine — check did not execute. That is an acceptable outcome, reported honestly, every time; producing a confident verdict on an unrun check is the one failure this protocol exists to make impossible

Two things that void a verdict silently, so check for them. Stale line numbers: every .claude/agents/*.md line citation in CANON_AUDIT.md is off by 9 because a banner was prepended to all ten files after the audit read them — re-locate every quote in the file as it is now, and a quote that no longer sits where it is cited is itself a finding. Quoting the worklist instead of the surface: the worklist's claim column is a transcription, so open the surface and confirm the text still reads that way, or the verdict is `cannot-determine — surface changed` with the current text quoted
